name: Alejandro A. Tagliavini
detail: Columnist in Panamá América (2019) against a billionaire tax.

name: José Antonio Pérez Barboni
detail: Independent deputy; his 2025 anteproyecto raises income-tax thresholds, sets higher income bands and cuts party tax breaks. An income tax, not a wealth tax.

name: Felipe Argote
detail: Economist; argues for ending large tax exemptions (exoneraciones) of the rich, not a tax on net wealth.

name: Rosario Arias Peña
detail: Universidad de Panamá economist; paper on the property tax (impuesto de inmuebles) and decentralisation. A property tax only.

name: Ley 526 de 2026 (economic substance, 15% on passive foreign income)
detail: Assembly (70 votes to 0) and President Mulino: 15% on multinational entities without substance; a corporate tax, not a wealth tax.

name: Edgar Cedeño (student centre president, Facultad de Derecho, Universidad de Panamá)
detail: Said in a university interview that the CSS reform should include taxes on grandes fortunas; a student representative speaking in passing, not a public figure with a position on record.

name: Marco A. Gandásegui, hijo
detail: CELA sociologist; 2009 and 2011 columns criticise tax cuts for the rich and subsidies, not a call for a tax on wealth. Reported dead in 2020.

name: Panamá América columnist, '¿Impuesto a la riqueza? ¡A los pobres!' (2020)
Panama as member of the PTLAC regional tax platform (May 2024)
detail: Press lists Panama among the platform's member countries, whose declaration backed Brazil's G20 billionaire-tax proposal; the communiqué does not list who signed and no Panamanian official statement was found.

name: Maribel Gordón
detail: Economist and 2024 presidential pre-candidate: calls the tax system regressive and evasion very high, wants a progressive system; no tax on wealth or fortunes in her interviews.

name: Juan Jované
detail: Economist; his CSS and economy interviews stress evasion of contributions and public works; no wealth-tax statement found.

name: Rafael Carles
detail: La Estrella columnist; piece on progressive versus regressive taxes concludes everyone should pay and the rich should take less from public resources; no tax on wealth proposed.
